therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: atherosclerotic plaque regression and cardiovascular event reduction
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with established cardiovascular disease and low HDL-C on statin therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Composite of CHD death, nonfatal MI, ischemic stroke, hospitalization for ACS, or symptom-driven coronary or cerebral revascularization

safety_signals: Higher rate of serious anaemia in ERN + Simvastatin arm (17/1718 vs 10/1696)
Higher rate of thrombocytopenia in ERN + Simvastatin arm (5/1718 vs 2/1696)
Trial stopped early due to lack of efficacy on recommendation of DSMB

dose_info.dose: 2000 mg/day (or 1500 mg/day if higher dose not tolerated) niacin; simvastatin dose adjusted to achieve LDL-C 40–80 mg/dL
dose_info.dose_modifications: Niacin dose reduced to 1500 mg/day if 2000 mg/day not tolerated; ezetimibe 10 mg/day added if needed to achieve LDL-C target

context.investigator_commentary: AIM-HIGH was stopped on the recommendation of the DSMB because of lack of efficacy of niacin in preventing primary outcome events.

results_by_chain.endpoint: Composite CHD death, nonfatal MI, ischemic stroke, ACS hospitalization, or revascularization
results_by_chain.mechanism_description: HDL elevation and triglyceride lowering via nicotinic acid receptor agonism
results_by_chain.biology_description: lipid profile modification and atherosclerotic plaque stabilization
results_by_chain.population_description: Patients with established cardiovascular disease and low HDL-C on background statin therapy

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Niacin was hypothesized to amplify simvastatin's cardiovascular protection by raising HDL-C and lowering triglycerides, complementing LDL-C reduction to further reduce atherosclerotic events
